result.topic_en: Latin draft from Riemann's Paris prize essay: the four-index expression (II) built from the quadratic form $\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$, its invariance and its vanishing for constant coefficients, the curvature measure (III) as a geometric interpretation, and the six conditions in the case n=3.
result.transcription:
$\delta\delta\sum b_{\iota\iota'}d s_\iota d s_{\iota'} - 2 d\delta \sum b_{\iota\iota'} d s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} + dd\sum b_{\iota\iota'}\delta s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'}$
[-variationi-] determinatis variationibus secundi ordinis $d^2, d\delta, \delta^2$ ita, ut sit.

[-pro-] denotante $d'$ variationem quamcunque. Quo pacto haec expressio invenietur
(II) $= \sum (\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''')(ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} - ds_{\iota'}\delta s_\iota)(ds_{\iota''}\delta s_{\iota'''} - ds_{\iota'''}\delta s_{\iota''})$
Jam ex hac [-ipsa-] formatione hujus expressionis sponte [-sequitur-] {+patet+}, mutatis variabilibus independentibus trans-
mutari [-eam-] in expressionem {+a+} nova forma ipsius $\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ eadem lege dependentem. At si quantitates $b$
sint constantes, omnes coefficientes expressionis (II) cifrae aequales evadunt. Unde si $\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in [-formam-]
expressionem similem constantibus coefficientibus affectam transformari potest, expressio II identice
evanescat necesse est.

[-Expressio $\sqrt{\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}}$ spectari potest tanquam elementum lineare in spatio generaliore $n$ dimensionum
nostrum intuitum transscendente.-]

Perinde patet [-expressionem-], si expressio II non evanescat, [-expressionem quantitatem-] [?]
(III) $\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\sum(\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''')\ldots}{\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'} \sum b_{\iota\iota'} \delta s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} - (\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'})^2}$
mutatis variabilibus independentibus non mutari insuperque immutatam manere si loco [-ipsarum-] {+variationum+} {+in+}
$ds_\iota, \delta s_\iota$ expressiones {+quaevis+} quaelibet lineares independentes [-harum quantitatum-] $\alpha ds_\iota + \beta\delta s_\iota$, $\gamma ds_\iota + \delta\delta s_\iota$ substituan-
tur. Valores autem maximi & minimi hujus functionis (III) ipsarum $ds_\iota, \delta s_\iota$ [-a forma ipsius $\sum b_{\iota\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$-]
neque a forma expressionis $\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$, neque a valoribus variationum $ds_\iota, \delta s_\iota$ pendebunt, unde ex his
valoribus dignosci poterit, an duae hujusmodi expressiones in se transformari possint.
[-Significationem geometricam harum disquisitionum obiter adiecisse juvabit.-]
Disquisitiones haece {+quodam+} interpretatione quadam geometrica illustrari possunt, quae quamquam conceptibus
inusitatis nitatur, tamen obiter eam addigitavisse juvabit.
Expressio $\sqrt{\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}}$ spectari potest tanquam elementum lineare in spatio generaliore $n$ dimen-
sionum nostrum intuitum transscendente. Quodsi in hoc spatio a puncto $(s_1, s_2 \ldots s_n)$ ducantur
omnes lineae brevissimae, in quarum elementis initialibus variationes ipsarum $s$ sunt ut $\alpha ds_1 + \beta\delta s_1$ :
$\alpha ds_2 + \beta\delta s_2$ : ... : $\alpha ds_n + \beta\delta s_n$ denotantibus $\alpha$ & $\beta$ quantitates quaslibet, [-obtinebitur superficies, quam-]
hae lineae superficiem constituunt, quam in spatium vulgare nostro intuitui subjectum evolvere licet.
Quo pacto expressio III erit mensura curvaturae hujus superficiei in puncto $(s_1, s_2 \ldots s_n)$
Si jam [-ad-] casum $n=3$ redimus, expressio II est forma secundi gradus ipsarum
$(ds_2\delta s_3 - ds_3\delta s_2)$, $ds_3\delta s_1 - ds_1\delta s_3$, $ds_1\delta s_2 - ds_2\delta s_1$
unde in hoc casu sex obtinemus aequationes, quibus functiones $b$ satisfacere debent, ut $\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$
in formam constantibus coefficientibus gaudentem transformari possit. [-Nec difficile est probatu-]
[-Commutatio responsionis quaestioni respondens ab Ill^{ma} Academia proposita:-]

methods.what: Combination of second variations of the quadratic form, defining the four-index expression
methods.quote: $\delta\delta\sum b_{\iota\iota'}d s_\iota d s_{\iota'} - 2 d\delta \sum b_{\iota\iota'} d s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} + dd\sum b_{\iota\iota'}\delta s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'}$
(II) $= \sum (\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''')(ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} - ds_{\iota'}\delta s_\iota)(ds_{\iota''}\delta s_{\iota'''} - ds_{\iota'''}\delta s_{\iota''})$

methods.what: Necessary condition for flatness: (II) vanishes identically if the form can be transformed to constant coefficients
methods.quote:
Unde si $\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in [-formam-]
expressionem similem constantibus coefficientibus affectam transformari potest, expressio II identice
evanescat necesse est.

methods.what: Sectional curvature expression (III), invariant under coordinate change and under change of basis of the plane
methods.quote: (III) $\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\sum(\iota\iota', \iota''\iota''')\ldots}{\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'} \sum b_{\iota\iota'} \delta s_\iota \delta s_{\iota'} - (\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota \delta s_{\iota'})^2}$

methods.what: Geometric interpretation: (III) is the Gaussian curvature of the surface formed by geodesics through a point in a 2-plane direction
methods.quote: Quo pacto expressio III erit mensura curvaturae hujus superficiei in puncto $(s_1, s_2 \ldots s_n)$

methods.what: For n=3, (II) is a quadratic form in three bivector components, giving six equations for flatness
methods.quote: unde in hoc casu sex obtinemus aequationes, quibus functiones $b$ satisfacere debent

items.quote:
Valores autem maximi & minimi hujus functionis (III) ipsarum $ds_\iota, \delta s_\iota$ [-a forma ipsius $\sum b_{\iota\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$-]
neque a forma expressionis $\sum b_{\iota\iota'} ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$, neque a valoribus variationum $ds_\iota, \delta s_\iota$ pendebunt, unde ex his
valoribus dignosci poterit, an duae hujusmodi expressiones in se transformari possint.
items.english: The maximum and minimum values of function (III) of $ds_\iota, \delta s_\iota$ depend neither on the form of the expression nor on the values of the variations, so from these values it can be recognized whether two such expressions can be transformed into each other.

items.quote: Ope notionum modo expositarum, est demonstrata, has sex conditiones, ut hoc fieri possit, sufficere.
items.english: By means of the notions just set out, it is demonstrated that these six conditions suffice for this to be possible.

items.quote: Observandum {+tamen+} est, tres tantum esse prorsus independentes.
items.english: It must however be observed that only three are fully independent.

items.english: Now, to fully solve the question proposed by the most illustrious Academy, into these six equations the forms of the functions $b$, found by the method set out above, are to be substituted...
